Subject: RFI: Sequence-level audit export & retention - details needed

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this RFI. Civic Bank is validating vendor capabilities around audit logs and sequence-level exportability for a planned pilot. We have a few concrete questions below — please provide as much technical detail as possible, and point us to any existing export samples/schema.

1) Retention windows: what are your default retention periods for audit/audit-trail logs in the hosted offering? Are retention windows configurable per-account or per-route? Maximum retention you support.

2) Export formats and ordering guarantees: when we request a "sequence export" for a conversation or stream, what formats are available (CSV/NDJSON/Parquet)? Do you guarantee ordering and monotonic sequence ids for message-level events?

3) Integrity & tamper-evidence: do you provide per-entry hashes, cumulative hashes (Merkle roots), or signed snapshots so we can verify exports for compliance?

4) Time stamps & timezone handling: are timestamps stored in UTC? do you include both server generation time and event-order sequence numbers?

5) Bulk export mechanics: API vs scheduled S3 dumps vs streaming (Kafka). What are typical latencies for exports (near-real-time vs 24/48h batch)?

6) Deleted/overwritten records: can exports include records that were deleted under regular deletion policies? Do you support legal-hold overrides?

7) Encryption & transport: are exports encrypted at rest and in transit; do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for exported artifacts?

We'd appreciate a sample export (schema + 10 sample lines, redacted) and an estimate for how long a full-history export for ~30M events would take.

Regards,
Ian Miller
Security Engineer, Civic Bank

Hi Ian / team —

I'm Karthik from Redwood's security and infra group — below are the concise, technical answers and the verification guidance. I also attached a short PDF that summarizes retention/exports for contractual language.

Retention windows
- Hosted (default): 180 days.
- Enterprise/Dedicated/Private: configurable per-account via policy; options: 1 year, 3 years, 5 years, up to 7 years on contractual terms.
- Retention scope: audit events, access logs, request/response metadata. Customers can request per-route overrides for high-sensitivity routes (e.g., payments).
- Legal hold: supported. When a legal hold is applied, normal deletion is suspended and we keep data until the hold is released.

Export formats & ordering
- Supported export formats: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON), Parquet (columnar), and CSV (for simple schemas). NDJSON is our canonical export format.
- Ordering & sequence: every event includes: event_id (UUIDv4), conversation_sequence (monotonic integer per conversation), global_sequence (monotonic across dataset), server_timestamp_utc (RFC3339 / ISO8601). We guarantee ordering as presented in the export per-conversation and maintain the global monotonicity for audit reproduction.

Integrity & tamper-evidence
- Per-entry: SHA-256 hash included for each exported event (field: entry_sha256).
- Daily checkpoint: we compute a Merkle root (SHA-256) across all export chunks for a UTC day and sign the root with our internal key. For enterprise customers we can also provide signed checkpoints using customer-managed keys via KMS for Dedicated/Private.
- Verification: we publish a verification tool in our SDK that validates per-entry hashes and the daily Merkle root; we'll include usage examples in the attached PDF.

Time handling
- All timestamps stored in UTC (server_timestamp_utc). Events also include client_provided_timestamp when available. We recommend using server_timestamp_utc for ordering.

Bulk export mechanics and latency
- Hosted: exports are generated as daily export jobs and available via signed S3 URLs (or direct download) within 24 hours of job completion. Full-history exports (multi-year) are queued and generally complete within 24-72 hours depending on size; for 30M events estimate: ~36-48 hours with default throughput.
- Dedicated/Private: options for near-real-time streaming to customer Kafka/S3 with per-event delivery within seconds, or continuous incremental exports.
- API bulk export: /v1/exports with pagination token; chunk size default 100k events per file; gzip/ndjson optional. Maximum parallel export workers configurable for Dedicated.

Deleted/overwritten records
- Exports respect retention and legal hold policies. If a record was deleted but retention window still in effect (e.g., soft-delete), it will be present in exports unless a final permanent-delete action outside retention has occurred. Legal hold preserves items beyond normal retention.

Encryption & keys
- In transit: TLS 1.2+/TLS1.3.
- At rest: AES-256.
- Customer-managed keys: supported for Dedicated & Private exports (KMS/HSM integration). Hosted customers may opt into a managed-KMS model with key separation controls.

Sample schema (NDJSON line example, redacted PII)
{
  "event_id": "3f9b8a6e-...",
  "global_sequence": 12598347,
  "conversation_sequence": 42,
  "server_timestamp_utc": "2026-11-30T16:00:12Z",
  "event_type": "inference.request",
  "actor": "user:REDACTED",
  "request_meta": {"prompt_hash": "sha256:...", "model": "redwood-13b-v2"},
  "entry_sha256": "e3b0c44298fc1c149..."
}

Verification steps (high-level)
1) Download NDJSON export file(s).
2) Run SDK verifier: checks entry_sha256 on each line and computes day's Merkle root.
3) Compare computed Merkle root to signed checkpoint we provide.

Operational notes
- Export retention on S3 signed URLs: 7 days by default (can be changed).
- We provide a sample CSV (attached) and a small Python script to demonstrate verification.
- SLA for on-demand retrieval jobs: standard request: 48h; expedited with SLA clause available on enterprise contract.

If helpful, we can provide a short PoC export (10k events) to your S3 bucket or a signed URL you control so you can run verification. Let me know preferred transport and whether you require customer-managed keys.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Security & Infra, Redwood Inference
